/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: ⟦G1⟧ is the natural connector between Jagalchi and ⟦G0⟧ — all three sit within the Nampo-dong cluster and can be walked end-to-end in under 10 minutes. Including ⟦G1⟧ as a standalone short stop (rather than passing through as a transit segment) acknowledges Busan's identity as **the host city of Asia's largest film festival** since 1996 — Korea's film industry has its public face here. The 25-minute stop fits the bus-tour pacing while giving guests time for one signature ssiat-hotteok and a walk past the most photographed director plaques. Designed-to-walk pedestrian street keeps the stop coach-friendly: the coach pre-positions toward the ⟦G0⟧ drop-off point while guests walk the corridor.

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/parking.source_en: No coach parking inside ⟦G1⟧ (pedestrian street); coach repositions toward ⟦G0⟧ while guests walk through

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/restroom.source_en: Lotte Department Store Gwangbok-ro Branch (free public restrooms) and CGV ⟦G0⟧ cinema lobby
/itineraryStops/5/convenience/restroom.tm: Универмаг Lotte на Кванбок-ро (бесплатные общественные уборные) и фойе кинотеатра CGV на ⟦G0⟧

/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
**⟦G1⟧ (비프광장, formerly PIFF Square)** is a 428-meter pedestrian corridor in Nampo-dong, Jung-gu, dedicated in **August 1996** to commemorate the launch of the **Busan International Film Festival (BIFF)** — Asia's largest film festival, first held that September. 

The square sits on what was historically **Korea's oldest cinema street**: the original **Bumin Theater opened here in 1924** and **Joongan Theater in 1927** during the Japanese colonial period, and the area has been the country's film exhibition heart ever since. 

The square's signature feature is **'Star Street'** — bronze-and-marble pavement plaques embedded with handprints, autographs, and birth years of internationally celebrated Korean directors and actors (Park Chan-wook, Bong Joon-ho, Kim Ki-duk, Im Kwon-taek, Choi Min-sik, and international guests including foreign film-festival jury members). 

At the Nampo-dong entrance stands the **PIFF Square ceremonial arch** that frames the square's most photographed angle. ⟦G1⟧ is also the birthplace of **'Ssiat Hotteok' (씨앗호떡)** — a Busan-specific variant of the Korean sweet pancake **'hotteok'** in which the doughy disc is split open after frying and stuffed with mixed seeds (sunflower, sesame, pumpkin, peanut) and brown sugar — a beloved Busan winter street food that has spread nationwide since the 2000s. 

Today the corridor is anchored by **CGV ⟦G1⟧**, **Daeyoung Cinema**, and **Megabox** screens, with adjacent **Lotte Department Store Gwangbok-ro** branch a one-minute walk away. 

**Free, open-air, 24-hour pedestrian street**; the busiest period is the **BIFF festival itself (10 days each October)** when temporary screens, red-carpet events, and director Q&As fill the corridor. 

On this bus-tour the visit is a short walk-through (~25 min) connecting Jagalchi to ⟦G0⟧ — sufficient for the ssiat-hotteok stop and a few handprint photos.

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/0.source_en: **Established 1945–1950** by post-liberation traders and **Korean War refugees** who fled south from North Korea

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/1.source_en: **Name 'Gukje (국제) = International'** — reflects the post-war black-market era when goods came from US troop PXs and worldwide aid imports
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/1.tm: **Название «Кукче (국제) = международный»** отражает послевоенную эпоху чёрного рынка, когда товары приходили из военторгов армии США и из мировой гуманитарной помощи

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.source_en: **~600 m × 100 m grid of 1,500+ stalls** — one of Korea's largest traditional markets
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.tm: **Сетка ~600 м × 100 м и более 1 500 прилавков** — один из крупнейших традиционных рынков Кореи

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/3.tm: **Шесть тематических рядов**: Arirang Street (одежда), Gongguk Street (посуда), Wood Street (пиломатериалы), Cosmetics Street, Hardware Street и Food Alley

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/4.source_en: Adjacent **Bupyeong Kkangtong Market** ('Tin Can Market') — Korea's first night market, popular for street food after sunset
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/4.tm: Соседний **рынок Пупхён Кканттон** («консервный рынок») — первый ночной рынок Кореи, популярный уличной едой после заката

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.source_en: Setting of the 2014 Korean film **'Ode to My Father' (⟦G0⟧)** — 14M ticket sales, anchored Korean War family-memory cinema
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.tm: Место действия корейского фильма 2014 года **«Ода моему отцу» (⟦G0⟧)** — 14 млн проданных билетов, опора кинематографа о семейной памяти Корейской войны

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.source_en: Hours typically 09:30–19:30 daily; many shops close **1st & 3rd Sundays** (varies by section)
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.tm: Часы работы обычно 09:30–19:30 ежедневно; многие лавки закрыты **в 1-е и 3-е воскресенье** (зависит от ряда)

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Bring **cash in small denominations** (₩1,000 and ₩5,000 notes) — most stalls don't take cards and prefer not to break ₩50,000 notes; light bargaining is normal at clothing and accessory stalls but not at food alleys; carry your own bag — disposable bags incur a fee
/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/tip.tm: Возьмите **наличные мелкими купюрами** (по ₩1 000 и ₩5 000): большинство прилавков не принимает карты и не любит разменивать ₩50 000. Лёгкий торг нормален у прилавков с одеждой и аксессуарами, но не в рядах с едой. Возьмите свою сумку — одноразовые пакеты платные.

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Public restrooms inside the adjacent Bupyeong Kkangtong building; ATMs along Daecheong-ro
/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.tm: Общественные уборные в соседнем здании Пупхён Кканттон; банкоматы вдоль Тэчхон-ро
